terms.comment: What something smells of is in the accusative: olet unguenta, “he smells of scent” (Ter.), crocum olēre (Cic. de Or. 3.99). Bene olēre, male olēre: to smell good, to smell bad.

terms.gloss: give off a scent, smell strongly of
evidence: Verg. G. 4.169: redolentque thymō frāgrantia mella

phrases.latin: et, ut mulierēs, ideō bene olēre quia nihil olēbant vidēbantur.
phrases.english: and, like women, they seemed to smell good precisely because they smelled of nothing.

phrases.latin: Postume, nōn bene olet quī bene semper olet.
phrases.english: Postumus, a man who always smells good doesn’t smell good.

phrases.latin: fīla Tarentīnī graviter redolentia porrī ēdistī quotiēns, ōscula clūsa datō.
phrases.english: whenever you’ve eaten threads of strong-smelling Tarentine leek, kiss with your mouth shut.

sources: Lewis & Short: oleo · Lewis & Short: redoleo
